title: Common-stage transition action and its counit mates
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, an algebraic closure $\Omega/\mathbf Q_\ell$, and schemes $X,Y$. For each subfield $i\subset\Omega$ finite over $\mathbf Q_\ell$ write $C_i(T)=D^b_c(T,i)$ and use actual scalar transitions $T_{ij}^T$ for $i\le j$. Let $C_\Omega(T)$ be the literal finite-field pair category with filtered-colimit Hom groups, $I_i^T:C_i(T)\to C_\Omega(T)$ the inclusions, and $\tau_{ij}^T:I_j^TT_{ij}^T\cong I_i^T$ the canonical transitions [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients, def-weil-rationalization-karoubi]. Thus a morphism from $(i,K)$ to $(j,L)$ is represented by $v_m:T_{im}^TK\to T_{jm}^TL$ at a common subfield $m\subset\Omega$ finite over $\mathbf Q_\ell$ and containing $i,j$.

Give adjunctions $F_i:C_i(X)\rightleftarrows C_i(Y):G_i$ and $F_\Omega:C_\Omega(X)\rightleftarrows C_\Omega(Y):G_\Omega$, with counits $\varepsilon_i,\varepsilon_\Omega$ [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate]. Give invertible scalar comparisons $q_{j/i}:T_{ij}^YF_i\cong F_jT_{ij}^X$ and $b_{j/i}:T_{ij}^XG_i\cong G_jT_{ij}^Y$ and common comparisons $q_i:I_i^YF_i\cong F_\Omega I_i^X$ and $b_i:I_i^XG_i\cong G_\Omega I_i^Y$. For each comparison $(q,b)$ along $T$, require the counit normalization
$$\varepsilon_{t,T^YL}F_t(b_L)q_{G_sL}=T^Y(\varepsilon_{s,L}).$$
Assume the rational $q_{j/i}$ obey the scalar associativity and identity equations with the actual scalar associators and unitors. Put
$$\delta_{i,m,K}=I_m^Y(q_{m/i,K})(\tau_{im,F_iK}^Y)^{-1}.$$
Require, for every common-stage representative, the actual arrow normalization
$$F_\Omega([m,v_m])=q_{j,L}\delta_{j,m,L}^{-1}I_m^Y(F_m(v_m))\delta_{i,m,K}q_{i,K}^{-1}.$$

Then for all $i\le j$, $K\in C_i(X)$ and $L\in C_i(Y)$ the given maps satisfy
$$q_{j,T_{ij}^XK}I_j^Y(q_{j/i,K})=F_\Omega((\tau_{ij,K}^X)^{-1})q_{i,K}\tau_{ij,F_iK}^Y,$$
$$b_{j,T_{ij}^YL}I_j^X(b_{j/i,L})=G_\Omega((\tau_{ij,L}^Y)^{-1})b_{i,L}\tau_{ij,G_iL}^X.$$
The equations use the pair-category endpoint identifications, so can be heterogeneous equalities in the formal record. They require no faithfulness of $I_i^T$ and no Karoubi completion. The inverse transition has its canonical identity representative at stage $j$ (with the identity-transition unitor); the displayed arrow normalization applies to that representative as well.

proof.text: Use the actual stage systems S_X,S_Y of [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]. The family F_i with beta=q_{j/i} is a StageSystem.Morphism H: S_X -> S_Y: its coherence field is exactly the assumed scalar_assoc equation. The already proved source-library quotient construction H.functor sends a representative v at m to q_{m/i} F_m(v) q_{m/j}^{-1}. Expand the representative hypothesis and mkHom_eq_isoToStage to obtain F_Omega([m,v]) = q_i^{-1} H.functor([m,v]) q_j. This is an equality of actual pair-category arrows, with no faithfulness or completion.

proof.text: The canonical transition tau^X_{ij,K} is represented at j by (S_X.assoc(h,refl)).hom_K. Calculate H.functor(tau^X_{ij,K}) = I_j(q_{j/i,K}^{-1}) tau^Y_{ij,F_i K}. To check this formula, expand functor_map_mkHom, the inclusion map, and transIso_hom_app_eq, and compose representatives at j. Cancel T^Y_jj(q_{j/i,K}); the remaining equation is precisely scalar_assoc(h,refl), followed by q q^{-1}=1. The helper pairFunctor_transition contains this calculation for arbitrary stage systems. Apply the preceding representative formula to tau^X and postcompose by F_Omega((tau^X)^{-1}); cancel the q and transition isomorphisms to obtain the required left comparison equation. This works for i=j without assuming a strict identity transition, and does not need scalar_unit.

proof.text: For L at stage i, let A and B be the left and right sides of the required right comparison equation and Q=I_j(q_{j/i,G_i L}) q_{j,T^X_ij G_i L}. Precompose the counit transpose F_Omega(A) epsilon_Omega by Q. Naturality of q_j at b_{j/i,L}, followed by common_counit at j and finite_counit at (i,j,L), gives I_j(T^Y_ij(epsilon_i,L)). This is the local equality ha in the Lean proof.

source.place: Extracted old common-stage and refinement-compatible adjunction argument, old steps 6 and 7; representative formula and counit transpose

proof.text: Rewrite Q using the left comparison equation, then compute Q F_Omega(B) epsilon_Omega. Functoriality cancels the adjacent inverse X transitions. Counit naturality at (tau^Y_ij,L)^{-1} and common_counit at i replace the middle composite by I_i(epsilon_i,L) (tau^Y_ij,L)^{-1}. Naturality of the inverse Y transition at epsilon_i,L then cancels tau^Y and its inverse. The result is again I_j(T^Y_ij(epsilon_i,L)). This is the local equality hb in Lean.

proof.text: Cancel the invertible Q in ha=hb. The two counit transposes are equal, so A=B by injectivity of (adjOmega.homEquiv _ _).symm, whose value is F_Omega(-) followed by epsilon_Omega. This is the objectwise counit-transpose bijection underlying [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate]. No morphism is canceled through a stage inclusion.

Step 4: Step 2 at G_iL, counit naturality at r_L, the normalization at i and naturality of tau^Y at eps_i give Phi(B)Q = I_jT(eps_i). Step 5: the transpose bijection, read as mateEquiv with alpha = Q^{-1} and side functors I_jT^X and I_jT^Y; this is the cited Mathlib leaf def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate. Both conclusions are the node's equations.
